novel_features.name: Openings watcher
novel_features.description: Get told the moment a spot frees up in a class or camp that is currently full.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local openings history to diff against; the API is present-tense only and the portal sends no notification of any kind.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this instead of re-polling a list endpoint yourself: it stores every observation, so it reports the transition rather than the current value.

novel_features.name: Catalog drift
novel_features.description: See what changed between syncs: classes and camps added, removed, retimed, or newly marked deleted.
novel_features.rationale: Compares two local snapshots; no upstream endpoint exposes history, an updated-at cursor, or a deletion feed.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to answer 'what is different since last week' without re-reading the whole catalog into context.

novel_features.name: Registration windows
novel_features.description: Find registration that has not opened yet or is about to close, across every synced class and camp.
novel_features.rationale: The registration date fields exist on every record but the API offers no filter on them and the portal surfaces none of them.
novel_features.why_it_matters: This is the only way to see a camp before its registration opens, which is when popular sessions are still winnable.

novel_features.name: Calendar export
novel_features.description: Export synced camps and classes to an RFC 5545 calendar file, one event per session.
novel_features.rationale: Builds events from the per-session schedule and block arrays; iClassPro publishes no feed in any format.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Turns a portal catalog into something a calendar app, a website, or a newsletter can consume directly.

novel_features.name: Tenant capability probe
novel_features.description: Report which surfaces an account actually exposes: open, sign-in-gated, or plan-gated.
novel_features.rationale: iClassPro signals both gates with HTTP 200 plus an explanatory message, so status codes alone cannot distinguish 'empty' from 'blocked'.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this first against any new account; it prevents mistaking a sign-in gate for a gym with no classes.

novel_features.name: Fill-rate trend
novel_features.description: Show how fast classes are filling over time, by class or by program.
novel_features.rationale: Aggregates the local openings history; a single API call can only ever report the current number.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers whether a class is trending toward full or toward cancellation, which no upstream call can express.

novel_features.name: Cross-tenant compare
novel_features.description: Compare the same kind of program across several gyms at once.
novel_features.rationale: Joins multiple synced tenants locally; program names and type ids differ per account, so no upstream call spans them.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Built for franchise and agency operators who track many gyms and need one table instead of many tabs.

novel_features.name: Catalog lint
novel_features.description: Flag catalog quality problems: missing descriptions or images, expired registration windows, deleted-but-listed programs.
novel_features.rationale: Checks fields the portal never validates, using the synced local copy so the whole catalog is inspected at once.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before publishing a schedule to a website; it catches the records that will render blank or dead.

narrative.headline: The only iClassPro tool that remembers yesterday — a queryable local mirror of any gym's catalog, with the search and filter surface the portal keeps to itself.
narrative.value_prop: iClassPro powers thousands of gymnastics, swim, dance, and cheer businesses and ships no developer API at all. This CLI treats the portal's own endpoints as one: it works against any account by its portal slug, keeps every sync in local SQLite, and answers the questions the upstream API structurally cannot — what changed since last week (drift), how fast a class is filling (fill-rate), and what registration opens next (opens-soon). It also exposes the filters the portal UI uses but nobody documented, including free-text search and openings-only.
narrative.auth_narrative: Most accounts need no credentials at all — the catalog endpoints answer plain HTTP with no key, no cookie, and no user agent. Some accounts set a portal flag that hides classes and camps behind a customer login; those return HTTP 200 with an empty list and a 'Please sign in to see classes.' message rather than an error. Run 'tenant <slug>' to find out which kind you are dealing with, and use 'auth login' to attach a read-only customer session when the gate is on. That session is replayed only on catalog reads: this CLI has no cart, enrollment, or checkout command.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the binary, config path, and local database are wired before touching the network
Find out whether this account is open, sign-in-gated, or plan-gated before assuming an empty result means empty
Every other command needs a location id, and this is where they come from
Free-text search plus openings-only, both honored server-side
Populate the local mirror; drift and fill-rate need at least two syncs before they can say anything
Registration opening or closing in the next two weeks, which the portal never shows

troubleshoots.symptom: classes list returns an empty array but the gym clearly has classes
troubleshoots.fix: Run 'iclasspro-pp-cli tenant <slug>' — the account probably hides its catalog behind customer sign-in, which the API reports as HTTP 200 with an empty list.

troubleshoots.symptom: A filter flag seems to do nothing and the result count never changes
troubleshoots.fix: Only --q, --openings, --programs, --levels, --instructors, --days, --ages, --genders, --sessions, --location-id, --limit and --page are honored upstream; anything else is applied locally and the CLI warns on stderr when it does so.

troubleshoots.symptom: camps list returns 'No camps found' for a type id that appeared in programs camps
troubleshoots.fix: Use 'bookings <slug> <locationId>' for type ids. The ids from 'programs camps' are programIds and never match --type-id.

troubleshoots.symptom: drift or fill-rate report nothing at all
troubleshoots.fix: Both read local history. Run 'iclasspro-pp-cli sync <account> --resources classes,camps' at least twice, spaced apart, before either has anything to compare.

troubleshoots.symptom: programs appointments returns a plan message instead of data
troubleshoots.fix: That account does not have the appointments subscription. The message is returned by iClassPro, not by this CLI, and there is no workaround.
The portal slug is wrong. It is the path segment in portal.iclasspro.com/<slug>, not the gym's brand name or website domain.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI whenever a task involves an iClassPro-powered business: gymnastics gyms, swim schools, dance and cheer studios. It is the right tool for reading a gym's class and camp catalog, searching or filtering it, watching for openings and registration windows, exporting schedules to a website or calendar, and comparing several gyms at once. It is especially suited to agencies and multi-location operators, because every command takes a portal slug and the local mirror can hold many accounts side by side. Prefer it over ad-hoc HTTP calls, because it knows which filters the API actually honors and which it silently ignores.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to enroll a student, add to a cart, apply a promo code, or pay — it is read-only by design and has no such commands.
Do not use it for staff-side operations like rosters, families, attendance, billing, or payroll; those live behind the iClassPro staff dashboard, which this CLI does not touch.
Do not use it to cancel or reschedule a booking on a family's behalf; direct the person to the customer portal.
Do not point it at a class-management product that is not iClassPro — Mariana Tek, Vagaro, Jackrabbit, and Sutra all have unrelated APIs.
Do not treat its output as a system of record for enrollment counts; openings is a portal-facing number, not the gym's roster.

recipes.title: Narrow a large class list down to just what an agent needs
recipes.explanation: Some gyms return well over a hundred classes with nested schedule arrays; selecting dotted paths keeps the payload small enough to reason over without paging through raw JSON.

recipes.title: Resolve camp type ids the correct way, then list that type
recipes.explanation: The booking menu is the only authoritative source of camp type ids; feeding a programId from 'programs camps' into --type-id silently returns nothing.

recipes.title: Publish a gym's camp schedule to a calendar file
recipes.explanation: Builds one event per camp session from the block and schedule arrays, with the portal registration link attached to each event.

recipes.title: Check several gyms for openings in one pass
recipes.explanation: Joins the synced copies of each account locally, which is the only way to line up programs whose names and ids differ per gym.

recipes.title: Audit a catalog before pushing it to a client website
recipes.explanation: Flags the records that will render blank or dead on a site: missing descriptions, missing images, expired registration windows, and programs already marked deleted upstream.
